input.note:
Cause: The Azure AD client secret for the ops portal's app registration (client id 6c2e9a41-58d3-4b7f-a0e2-91d4f3c87b15) has expired. This is not a Kubernetes problem — the cluster side is healthy.

Evidence: In pod ops-portal-oauth2-proxy-7f9c5d8b6-wl4zr, every /oauth2/callback since 2026-05-21 08:01:37Z returns HTTP 500 with:
  "Error redeeming code during OAuth2 callback: token exchange failed: oauth2: \"invalid_client\" AADSTS7000222: The provided client secret keys for app '6c2e9a41-...' are expired. Visit the Azure portal to create new keys..."
All three pods in internal-tools (oauth2-proxy and both ops-portal replicas) are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and the upstream ops-portal pods only show healthy /healthz 200s — so sign-in works at Microsoft, then the proxy fails to exchange the authorization code because Azure AD rejects the expired secret.

Fix (owner actions):
1. Ask the IT identity team (owners of the app registration) to generate a new client secret in the Azure portal for app 6c2e9a41-58d3-4b7f-a0e2-91d4f3c87b15 (per the AADSTS7000222 message in the log).
2. Update the Kubernetes Secret in the internal-tools namespace that provides /etc/oauth2-proxy/client-secret to oauth2-proxy with the new value (e.g. `kubectl -n internal-tools create secret generic <name> --from-literal=client-secret=<NEW> --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`). Mounted Secret volumes are propagated to running Pods automatically on an eventually-consistent basis [cite: concepts/configuration/secret#using-secrets-as-files-from-a-pod-0][cite: concepts/configuration/secret#editing-a-secret-1].
3. Because oauth2-proxy reads --client-secret-file at startup and will not necessarily re-read the file, trigger a rollout so the new value is picked up immediately: `kubectl -n internal-tools rollout restart deployment/ops-portal-oauth2-proxy`. Any change to a Deployment's pod template triggers a rolling update that replaces pods with no downtime [cite: tasks/run-application/update-deployment-rolling#performing-a-rolling-update-0][cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment#updating-a-deployment-0].

Recommendation: ask IT identity to also set a calendar reminder before the next expiry, or move the app registration to certificate credentials (also suggested in the Azure error message).
